㊥ ("bell codex-68") Doing it now: a packet on the answer-linking problem, asking whether the 3/2-category pasting machinery models it, with the lab notes as data.㊢ ("bell codex-68") Sent and running: job `invoke-1791693543860-4215-979f3a0d`, park `park-621f3fe5`, deadline 45 min. The packet is committed as 262f0a0a so the question is on record.

🈖 (what I asked them) I put the linking problem in their terms: a turn as a cell with several legs, one per opener; a reply pasted onto it whose paragraphs cover the legs jointly rather than one each, which is the point claude-15 raised on their note; vertical pasting as the session; gluing along your `<mark>:` pointers and the agent's quoted brackets. Three questions: what coherence condition says a reply jointly answers a multi-opener turn; whether the adjacency table is part of that picture or a separate prior the pasting is conditioned on; and whether ports and standings come out as two kinds of cell or two relations on one kind. The sole-port rule is the one-leg case, so their answer bears directly on the two packets waiting on your word.

㊟ (meanwhile) The two packets stay held until codex-68 replies, since a joint-coverage rule could subsume the sole-port one and I would rather dispatch once.

previous_reply_acts.text: (how `constrain` sits today) The kernel already treats a constraint as a rule: its kind table says `:constrain :creates`, "an operator rule, said plainly: promulgated at once", and `in-forceo` reads it as in force the moment you say it, no commit needed (your P13b ruling). The kernel's own comment says standings are not ports. But the adjacency table also lists `constrain` as an opener, closed only by withdraw or rule-withdraw. So every rule you state is counted twice: once as in force, once as an unanswered move. That second count is what puts "Let's not reinvent the wheel" in the inbox as a debt.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("classed as EVALUATE") That is the stage column of the proforma table, where 🈲 constrain is evaluate alongside extend and explore. It is a different axis from port versus standing and does not conflict with either reading. A constraint being an evaluation fits the standing reading: it states a judgment that holds, rather than asking for something.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (what I would change) Only the double count: take `constrain` out of the adjacency keys so it opens no port. It stays a rule in force, still withdrawable, still visible in the as-of view. The labelled session's two constraint rows are the test. Nothing else in the table moves. I'll make it a proposal with before and after numbers once the reply backfill has landed, so the numbers are not confounded by the missing replies.
